qc_chibougamau.blurb: Chibougamau is a small group of cliffs in the Jamesie region of northern Quebec, centered on the Mont Bedard crags. The walls run roughly 15 to 50 meters tall, and the climbing is mostly bolted sport with a few trad lines and some top-rope options. Grades stretch from easy 5.7 all the way to 5.13, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper, technical routes more than beginners. The cliffs are reached by a sizeable walk along a signed ATV trail, so plan a fuller day than a roadside crag would need. Several of the harder lines have seen few repeats, so treat their grades as provisional.

qc_07_grand_canyon.blurb: Grand Canyon is one of the busiest sectors at Montagne d'Argent, a climbing park in La Conception in the Laurentides, a couple of hours north of Montreal. The park works much like an outdoor gym: most routes are single pitch, anchors are bolted for easy lowering or rappel, and walking to the top makes setting up a top-rope simple. This sector mixes trad and sport lines, with grades running from low 5th class to 5.12 and the majority falling between 5.7 and 5.10, a good fit for climbers building experience. Popular sectors like this one can feel crowded when clubs and groups are out.

qc_f_black_white_club_sandwich.blurb: This is the right-hand end of the big Weir cliff on Mont Larose in the Laurentides. The sector began mostly as aid climbing, and many of those lines have since gone free, with newer routes pushing the difficulty. The climbing is a blend of trad and sport, ranging from a 5.7 up to 5.13, though most routes fall between 5.11 and 5.13, so it is mainly a place for experienced climbers. The upper right side holds hard lines and projects that start from a small ledge reached by an easier route. It sees less traffic than the rest of the cliff. A signed trail leads in, and early in the season ice can fall from above.

ri_great_slab_wave_boulder.blurb: One of the best-known clusters at Lincoln Woods, the state park bouldering area just north of Providence. Locals call it either the Great Slab, after the slab visible from the road, or the Wave, after its most famous problem. Nearly all the problems are on the easier side, with the majority between V0 and V4 and a handful of harder ones climbing to V8, which makes it a good warm-up spot and a fine place for newer boulderers. The stone is coarse and sharply textured, so friction is best in cool, crisp weather; summer days get humid. Sunny winter days often stay climbable here when other areas are buried.

sd_turtle_dome.blurb: Turtle Dome sits on Iron Mountain in the Black Hills, in the Needles of Rushmore. It is mostly granite bouldering, part of the second-largest concentration of established boulder problems in the Black Hills, with a few roped trad and sport lines around the dome. Problems tend to be short and moderate, though the range runs from easy V0 up through V10 and beyond, so there is something for a wide spread of abilities. The boulders lie below the dome across from the Rubik's Ridge group, and the trail in is faint and hard to follow, so allow time to find your way. Iron Mountain is a good choice when busier Needles areas feel crowded.

sd_dark_side_wall.blurb: Dark Side Wall is the main wall of the Dark Side, a sport crag in Spearfish Canyon in the northern Black Hills. Every route is bolted sport, and almost all fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with a few 5.13s, so this is a venue for strong climbers. The rock is solid limestone with blonde and dark streaked bands. A few stout 5.11s on the section with the pale base make a good way to start, with harder lines farther down canyon and a shorter wall up the slope that still packs a punch. The Dark Side is known as a shady refuge on hot summer days.
